title: WM-MT147-PostMergeReclaim
clause: Post-merge lifecycle: worktree removal, session branch deletion per policy, VM snapshot/reclaim via WorktreeVmRegistry, CLEANUP-FAILED surfacing, bounded logged orphan sweep

scope.summary:
GOAL: Close the resource lifecycle after a governed merge succeeds (MT-145 Executed): remove the session worktree, delete the session branch per the reclaim policy, snapshot-then-reclaim the worktree microVM, surface any cleanup failure through the existing FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED event, and provide a BOUNDED, LOGGED orphan sweep for merged-but-unreclaimed worktrees so leaks are visible and recoverable, never silent. Today cleanup_session_worktree (workspace_safety.rs ~418-440) removes a worktree with `worktree remove --force` under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK but knows nothing about merge state or branches, MT-141 added cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy + the KeepUntilMerged/DeleteOnReclaim SessionBranchReclaimPolicy (default KeepUntilMerged), and WorktreeVmRegistry (worktree_vm_registry.rs) exposes snapshot ~117 / restore ~134 / teardown_worktree_vm ~215 but nothing ties them to merge completion.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New reclaim functions in src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_safety.rs (next to cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy) plus a bounded orphan-sweep function; a small async reclaim helper coupling the git reclaim to WorktreeVmRegistry snapshot+teardown. FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED (success) and FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED (failure) are REUSED (events.rs SwarmFrEventId lines 75-78); NO new FR kinds. Tests under the handshake_core test tree.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Types (workspace_safety.rs):
   pub struct PostMergeReclaimPlan { pub session_id: String, pub worktree_path: PathBuf, pub branch: Option<String>, pub reclaim_policy: SessionBranchReclaimPolicy, pub vm_worktree_id: Option<String>, pub merged_into: String }  // merged_into = the target branch the session merged into (used to VERIFY merge before deleting the branch)
   pub enum ReclaimFailure { WorktreeRemove { error: String }, BranchDelete { branch: String, error: String }, VmReclaim { worktree_id: String, error: String } }
   pub enum PostMergeReclaimOutcome { Reclaimed { branch_deleted: bool, vm_snapshotted: bool, vm_reclaimed: bool }, PartiallyReclaimed { done: Vec<String>, failures: Vec<ReclaimFailure> }, Skipped { reason: String } }
2. Reclaim function:
   pub async fn reclaim_after_merge(repo_root: &Path, plan: &PostMergeReclaimPlan, vm_registry: Option<&WorktreeVmRegistry>) -> PostMergeReclaimOutcome
   Order (each step independent; a failure records a ReclaimFailure and continues to the next, ending PartiallyReclaimed — reclaim is best-effort and never panics a merge that already succeeded):
   a. MERGE VERIFICATION before any branch deletion: confirm the session branch is an ancestor of merged_into via `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <merged_into>` (exit 0). If NOT merged, do NOT delete the branch (Skipped/kept) — deletion only ever follows proven merge.
   b. VM snapshot + reclaim (when vm_registry + vm_worktree_id present): snapshot FIRST (vm_registry.snapshot -> SnapshotRef, portable recoverable state) THEN vm_registry.teardown_worktree_vm; a snapshot failure aborts the teardown (never tear down un-snapshotted state) and records VmReclaim failure.
   c. Worktree removal: cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy(repo_root, worktree_path, policy) (MT-141) under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK.
   d. Branch deletion: ONLY when reclaim_policy == DeleteOnReclaim AND (a) proved merged: `git -C <repo_root> -c core.longpaths=true branch -d <branch>` (MT-141 path, -d NEVER -D — a still-unmerged branch fails closed and is surfaced, never force-deleted). KeepUntilMerged leaves the branch.
   e. Emit FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED on success (payload: session_id, branch, branch_deleted, vm_snapshotted, vm_reclaimed) and FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED for each ReclaimFailure (payload: session_id, worktree_id, stage, error) through the existing SwarmEventSink; reuse the SwarmFrEventId ids (events.rs 75-78) — if the emitting SwarmEvent variant for worktree reclaim/cleanup was added by MT-141 reuse it, else add a WorktreeReclaimed/WorktreeCleanupFailed SwarmEvent variant carrying the payload, still with NO new FrEventId string.
3. Orphan sweep:
   pub async fn sweep_orphaned_merged_worktrees(repo_root: &Path, target_branches: &[String], max_reclaim: usize, vm_registry: Option<&WorktreeVmRegistry>) -> OrphanSweepReport
   - Enumerate session worktrees via `git -C <repo_root> worktree list --porcelain`; for each session/<id> worktree whose branch is an ancestor of some target (merge-base --is-ancestor) but still present, it is a merged-but-unreclaimed ORPHAN.
   - Reclaim orphans up to max_reclaim (BOUNDED — never an unbounded sweep), building a PostMergeReclaimPlan per orphan and calling reclaim_after_merge; LOG every considered/reclaimed/skipped orphan (structured log line) and every failure via CLEANUP-FAILED.
   - OrphanSweepReport { scanned: usize, reclaimed: usize, skipped: usize, failures: Vec<ReclaimFailure>, hit_bound: bool } so a leak trend is observable; hit_bound=true means more orphans remain than max_reclaim (surface, do not silently drop).
4. HARD RULES: branch deletion is `git branch -d` only (fail-closed on unmerged), NEVER -D / --force; VM state is SNAPSHOTTED before teardown (recoverable, portable evidence — pairs with the MT-144 patch-bundle recovery path); the sweep is bounded + fully logged (no unbounded/silent cleanup); worktree code reclaim is strictly separate from CRDT document state (kernel/crdt untouched); every git invocation carries -c core.longpaths=true under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK for worktree/branch mutation.
5. BOUNDARY: this MT reclaims resources AFTER a proven merge; it does not merge, does not decide policy (MT-145 does), and does not push/fetch. It reuses MT-141 (cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy, SessionBranchReclaimPolicy, branch -d) and the WorktreeVmRegistry as-is.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read workspace_safety.rs cleanup_session_worktree (~418-440), the MT-141-added cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy + SessionBranchReclaimPolicy, session_worktree_path (~356), SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK; worktree_vm_registry.rs snapshot ~117 / teardown_worktree_vm ~215; events.rs SwarmFrEventId WorktreeReclaimed/WorktreeCleanupFailed (75-78) + the SwarmEventSink emit path.
2. Add the PostMergeReclaimPlan / ReclaimFailure / PostMergeReclaimOutcome types.
3. Implement reclaim_after_merge with the merge-verification-before-delete order, snapshot-before-teardown VM handling, and per-stage failure recording.
4. Implement sweep_orphaned_merged_worktrees with the porcelain scan, ancestor test, bound, and structured logging + OrphanSweepReport.
5. Wire FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED / -CLEANUP-FAILED emission (reuse ids; reuse or add the SwarmEvent payload variant without a new FrEventId).
6. Tests (scratch git repo + fake WorktreeVmRegistry adapter, same FakeVmAdapter shape as worktree_vm_registry.rs tests): merged branch + DeleteOnReclaim => worktree removed, branch deleted, RECLAIMED emitted; KeepUntilMerged => worktree removed, branch KEPT; UNMERGED branch + DeleteOnReclaim => branch NOT deleted (fails closed), Skipped/kept + surfaced; VM snapshot failure => teardown NOT attempted, VmReclaim failure recorded, CLEANUP-FAILED emitted; worktree-remove failure => PartiallyReclaimed + CLEANUP-FAILED; orphan sweep over N merged orphans with max_reclaim=k reclaims exactly k and reports hit_bound=true with (N-k) remaining.
7. Run proof targets; record measured output.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs (reuse WORKTREE-RECLAIMED/-CLEANUP-FAILED ids; payload/variant only, NO new FrEventId)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (GUI IPC allowed only on the GUI MT, MT-146)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain; do not conflate with git worktree code merge)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (merge engine is MT-142; reclaim happens after it, not inside it)
acceptance_criteria: reclaim_after_merge verifies the session branch is merged into merged_into (`merge-base --is-ancestor`) BEFORE any branch deletion; an unmerged branch is never deleted.

Branch deletion uses `git branch -d` only (MT-141 path); a live test proves an unmerged branch under DeleteOnReclaim fails closed and survives, surfaced as a failure/Skipped, with zero '-D'/'--force' in the reclaim code.
VM reclaim snapshots FIRST then tears down via WorktreeVmRegistry; a snapshot failure aborts teardown (un-snapshotted state is never destroyed) and records a VmReclaim ReclaimFailure.
Worktree removal reuses cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy (MT-141) under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK with -c core.longpaths=true.
KeepUntilMerged (default) removes the worktree but KEEPS the branch; DeleteOnReclaim removes the worktree AND deletes the proven-merged branch.
Reclaim is best-effort: a failure in any stage records a ReclaimFailure and continues, returning PartiallyReclaimed, and never unwinds a merge that already succeeded.

Success emits FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED and each failure emits FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED through the existing SwarmEventSink, reusing the events.rs ids (lines 75-78) with NO new FrEventId string.

sweep_orphaned_merged_worktrees is BOUNDED by max_reclaim and LOGS every considered/reclaimed/skipped orphan; OrphanSweepReport reports scanned/reclaimed/skipped/failures/hit_bound so leaks are observable, never silent.
Every git invocation added by this MT includes -c core.longpaths=true; worktree/branch mutation holds SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK.

src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs (REUSE ids: WorktreeReclaimed/WorktreeCleanupFailed lines 75-78; SwarmEventSink emit path; NO new FrEventId)

scratch-repo: KeepUntilMerged => worktree removed, branch KEPT
scratch-repo: unmerged branch + DeleteOnReclaim => branch NOT deleted (fails closed), surfaced, branch still exists

implementation_notes: MT-141 reuse is load-bearing: cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy, SessionBranchReclaimPolicy (KeepUntilMerged default), and the `git branch -d` fail-closed path all come from MT-141; this MT orchestrates them after merge and adds the VM + sweep, so despite depends_on listing MT-142/MT-145 the MT-141 primitives must exist in the implementing worktree.

Snapshot-before-teardown makes a lost VM recoverable and pairs with MT-144's ledgered patch bundle: between the snapshot and the patch bundle, merged session state is never stranded on a torn-down VM.

Merge verification uses git's own ancestry (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), not a cached merged flag, so a branch is deleted only when git itself proves it merged — belt-and-braces with the `branch -d` fail-closed safety.
The orphan sweep is a leak DETECTOR + bounded janitor, not an unbounded GC: hit_bound surfaces backlog so an operator/scheduler runs it again rather than the sweep quietly churning.
Reclaim is best-effort and non-fatal: a merge already committed must not be undone by a cleanup hiccup; failures are recorded + emitted, not propagated as merge failures.
Do not introduce push/fetch: reclaim is local worktree/branch/VM lifecycle only.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend post-merge lifecycle; reclaim outcomes and orphan-sweep leaks are reconstructable from FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED / -CLEANUP-FAILED events and the OrphanSweepReport log (TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004). Operator-visible merge state is MT-146.

target_entries: Worktrees > Post-merge reclaim (worktree removal, branch deletion per reclaim policy, VM snapshot+reclaim)
Worktrees > Orphan sweep (bounded reclaim of merged-but-unreclaimed worktrees; reading the sweep report and CLEANUP-FAILED events)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Reuse FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-RECLAIMED (success) and FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED (each ReclaimFailure) through the existing SwarmEventSink; no new kinds. The orphan sweep additionally emits CLEANUP-FAILED per failed orphan.

Emit a diagnostic event on a VM snapshot/teardown error or a worktree-remove error via the open diagnostic-event API if present; else DEFERRED-with-reason. The OrphanSweepReport hit_bound is a structured-log diagnostic of backlog.
Reclaim is bounded git subprocesses + a snapshot call; the microVM's own liveness is the WorktreeVmRegistry's concern, not this reclaim path.

risk_if_missed: Merged session worktrees, branches, and microVMs pile up unreclaimed: disk and VM slots leak, refs/heads fills with dead session branches, and lost-but-merged VM state is stranded with no recovery — the swarm silently degrades until it cannot spawn, with no visible signal.

risks: RISK-1: A session branch is deleted before it is actually merged (trusting a stale merged flag instead of git ancestry), destroying unmerged agent commits with no recovery.
RISK-2: Branch deletion uses -D / --force to 'just clean up', force-deleting an unmerged branch and losing work — the exact failure `branch -d` fail-closed exists to prevent.
RISK-3: The microVM is torn down before (or without) a snapshot, so a worktree whose merge later needs re-examination has no recoverable live state.
RISK-4: A reclaim failure propagates and unwinds or masks a merge that already succeeded, or fails silently so the leak is invisible (no CLEANUP-FAILED event).
RISK-5: The orphan sweep runs unbounded / unlogged, either churning the whole repo under the git lock or hiding a growing backlog with no signal.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Deletion is gated on `merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <merged_into>` exit 0 at reclaim time; a test with an unmerged branch proves the branch is kept, not deleted.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Deletion path is `git branch -d` only (MT-141); grep proof target asserts no '-D'/'--force-with-lease' in the reclaim code, and the unmerged-branch test proves fail-closed survival.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): VM reclaim snapshots first and aborts teardown on snapshot failure; a fake-adapter test asserts teardown is NOT called when snapshot errors, and vm_snapshotted precedes vm_reclaimed in the success payload.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Reclaim is best-effort and non-throwing: each stage records a ReclaimFailure + emits CLEANUP-FAILED and continues to PartiallyReclaimed; a test injects a worktree-remove failure and asserts the merge is untouched and the failure is emitted (not silent).

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): The sweep is hard-bounded by max_reclaim, logs every considered/reclaimed/skipped orphan, and reports hit_bound with the remaining count; a test with N>k orphans asserts exactly k reclaimed and the backlog surfaced.

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 src/backend/handshake_core/src/workspace_safety.rs cleanup_session_worktree ~418-440 (`git worktree remove --force` under SESSION_WORKTREE_GIT_LOCK with -c core.longpaths=true), session_worktree_path ~356, collect_merge_back_artifact ~331; swarm_orchestration/worktree_vm_registry.rs snapshot ~117 / restore ~134 / teardown_worktree_vm ~215 (persistent CH microVM, TOCTOU-safe); swarm_orchestration/events.rs SwarmFrEventId WorktreeReclaimed/WorktreeCleanupFailed lines 75-78 + SwarmEventSink emit path. MT-141 supplies cleanup_session_worktree_with_policy, SessionBranchReclaimPolicy (KeepUntilMerged default), and the `git branch -d` fail-closed path this MT orchestrates. Field practice: post-merge branch cleanup gated on merged-ancestry (git's `branch -d` refusal on unmerged) is the standard safe-delete idiom; snapshot-before-teardown mirrors VM checkpoint-then-reclaim so state loss is recoverable; a bounded, reported janitor sweep is the field pattern for leak-detecting GC rather than unbounded churn.
corrections: Operator/red-team hard rules baked in: branch deletion only after git-proven merge and only with `branch -d` (never -D/--force); VM snapshotted before teardown so merged state stays recoverable; orphan sweep bounded + fully logged (no silent/unbounded cleanup).
Reclaim is best-effort and never unwinds a completed merge; failures surface via FR-EVT-SWARM-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-FAILED (reused id, no new kind).
